methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $46M total raised proxy.

private.name: Material Evolution
private.rationale: Same sector (Housing & Construction), same stage (Series A)

data.narrative:
Cobod, a Series A–stage housing and construction technology company founded by Henrik Lund-Nielsen, has raised $46M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a single private comparable (Material Evolution) and no public peers, reflecting the nascent nature of the frontier-tech construction sector.

The stage-progression method provides the primary valuation anchor. Applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier—typical for Series A to subsequent-stage advancement—to the $46M total raised proxy yields $92M. This methodology assumes capital deployment efficiency and market validation consistent with progression expectations but is constrained by limited observable market data for comparable construction-tech exits.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $78M to $106M, with a median of $92M. The relatively narrow band reflects the single-method approach and constrained comparable universe. Key uncertainties include: the representativeness of Material Evolution as a peer (sector, stage, and capital structure alignment remain underspecified), the applicability of standard stage-progression multiples in an emerging technology domain, and the absence of public market reference points. Future valuation refinement would benefit from expanded private comparable data and clearer articulation of Cobod's differentiation within the construction-tech landscape.
